1.explanation: The root of the bug lives in the LaTeX grammar definition in src/languages/latex.js. The object COMMAND (and by extension the formula variant) includes a sub-mode labelled className: 'string' that begins on /\{/ and ends on /\}/. When highlight.js enters that mode, it treats the entire brace-delimited block as a string and does not apply further TeX or math highlighting to its contents. To fix this, the braces variant either must be removed or replaced so that content inside { … } is lexed normally (i.e. sub-parsed with the standard COMMAND and formula rules) rather than locked into a flat string mode.
1.bug_scenario: In highlight.js’s LaTeX grammar, everything between literal “{” and “}” is treated as a “string” mode. As a result, any valid TeX commands or math (e.g. \eTiX, \pi, \!, \~, superscripts, text macros) that appear inside braces are never fed back into the normal command or formula highlighter. The screenshots show braces such as {x^3}, {Hello \! world}, and {Goodbye\~ world} rendered with no syntax highlighting of the TeX content inside.

2.explanation: The COMMAND mode in src/languages/latex.js defines LaTeX commands and then contains a sub-mode with className 'string' whose variants begin/end on '{' and '}'. That mode greedily consumes all text inside braces as a single string, preventing nested commands from being highlighted. The default export function builds the overall language definition, so the fix must adjust or remove the '{…}' string variant in COMMAND to allow normal parsing inside braces.
2.bug_scenario: In the provided screenshots of LaTeX code, any code inside curly braces (e.g. ‘{…}’) is highlighted as a single string‐like block, so commands such as \eTiX, \TeX, \!, \~ and other LaTeX constructs inside those braces never receive their normal syntax highlighting. Everything between ‘{’ and ‘}’ is treated as a ‘string’ and its inner tokens are ignored.
